description: Inspired by information-theoretic branch-and-prune algorithms (Ahmed et al. 2023), we propose using information gain metrics to order Collatz bit-tree exploration. Instead of DFS, use the 'dip' value as priority: explore low-dip branches first to find survivors quickly for GPU dispatch, overlapping CPU recursion with GPU computation.
mathematical_formalization: Information gain of branch b: IG(b) ~ -log2(density(BV_{f-f_min})). Priority queue: explore branches with highest expected survival first. Pipeline overlap: launch GPU kernel when 2^16 survivors accumulated.
analogical_connections: Huffman coding — assign shorter codes to more common events
implementation_hypothesis: Replace DFS with priority queue ordered by (f - f_min, current_dip). Process low-dip-high-f branches first. Launch GPU kernels asynchronously when batches of 2^16 are ready.
experiment_seed: Compare DFS vs priority-queue orderings. Measure GPU utilization, wall-clock time, peak memory.
